Issue Summary:
The IDF switch (.41) went offline due to a loss of uplink connectivity to the MDF switch (.40).

Troubleshooting Performed:

* On the MDF switch (.40), uplink port Gi1/0/48, which connects to switch .41, showed no link lights.
* The uplink cable was reseated on both ends, but no link was established.
* On the IDF switch (.41), the corresponding uplink port Gi1/0/48 also showed no link lights.
* The IDF switch was rebooted, and the uplink cable was reseated again, but the issue persisted.
* To rule out a faulty switch port, the uplink cable on the MDF switch was moved from port Gi1/0/48 to Gi1/0/35. The alternate port also failed to establish a link.
* Based on the troubleshooting results, attention shifted to the physical cabling between the MDF and IDF switches.

Resolution:

* The cabling between the MDF and IDF switches was replaced.
* After the cable replacement, link connectivity was immediately restored between the switches.
* The uplink came back online, and the IDF switch (.41) returned to normal operation.

Root Cause:
The issue was caused by a faulty cable run between the MDF and IDF switches, which prevented the uplink ports from establishing a physical link.

Current Status:
Resolved. The uplink is operational, and the IDF switch is online and functioning normally.
